A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fe K emission in these galaxies can be explained by either a starburst or an AGN, but it is unlikely to be produced in a star-forming galaxy with a normal initial mass function.
the Fe K line is not a reliable indicator of the presence of an AGN.
the X-ray quietness is a common property for ULIRGs, and it is not a result of a small sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that
luminous infrared galaxies are not simply scaled-up versions of nearby star-forming systems, as is often assumed.

the X-ray properties of luminous infrared galaxies depend strongly on their infrared properties and that they are not a single population of galaxies with a single X-ray spectral energy distribution, but rather a mixture of different populations.
